account.question: Do I need an account?
account.answer: No. You can add birthdays right away without signing in. Sign in with Google when you want to keep them in your account.

storage.question: Where are my birthdays stored?
storage.answer: Without an account, birthdays are saved in this browser only. After you sign in with Google, they are stored in your account, and the birthdays you added before signing in can be moved there.

phone.question: Does it work on my phone?
phone.answer: Yes. Birthdly works in any modern mobile browser, and you can add it to your home screen to open it like an app.

addBirthday.question: How do I add a birthday?
addBirthday.answer: Open the calendar, press the + button, and enter a name and a date.

noYear.question: Can I add a birthday without the birth year?
noYear.answer: Yes. Leave the year empty, and Birthdly shows the birthday every year without the age.

reminders.question: Will Birthdly remind me about birthdays?
reminders.answer: Yes. Sign in with Google and turn on birthday notifications in Settings. You get a notification on the day, the day before, or both, at the time you choose, without keeping Birthdly open.

googleCalendar.question: Can I sync birthdays with Google Calendar?
googleCalendar.answer: Yes. Sign in with Google and connect Google Calendar in Settings. Birthdly shows your birthdays in Google Calendar and brings in birthdays from your Google contacts.

googleCalendarBirthdays.title: How to add birthdays to Google Calendar
googleCalendarBirthdays.description: Add birthdays to Google Calendar as yearly birthday events with a reminder the day before, and keep them in sync with Birthdly.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text01: Google Calendar is where many people already plan their week, so it is a natural place for birthdays too. This guide shows two ways to get birthdays into Google Calendar: by hand in Google, and automatically with Birthdly, which keeps them in sync for you.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text03: Google Calendar has a special kind of event for birthdays. It is an all-day event that repeats every year and appears with a cake icon. Google creates these events on its own for the people in your Google Contacts who have a birthday saved, so if a friend's birthday is in their contact card, you will usually see it in your calendar already.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text04: For everyone else, such as colleagues, neighbors, or relatives you never saved as contacts, Google Calendar shows nothing until you add the birthday yourself.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text06: There are two common ways to do it without any extra tools.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text07: Add the birthday to a contact
googleCalendarBirthdays.text08: Open Google Contacts and find the person, or create a new contact.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text09: Choose Edit, add the Birthday field, and enter the date. The year is optional.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text10: Save the contact. The birthday appears in Google Calendar as a yearly birthday event.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text12: In Google Calendar, create an all-day event on the birthday with the person's name as the title.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text13: Set it to repeat annually and add a notification, for example one day before.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text15: Both work, but they get tedious with more than a handful of people. Contacts fill up with entries you only need for a date, and repeating events are easy to get wrong, especially for someone born on February 29.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text17: Sign in with Google. Use the account button in the top right corner. Birthdays you added before signing in can be moved to your account.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text18: Connect Google Calendar. Open Settings, find the Google Calendar card, and press Connect Google Calendar. Google shows two permissions: to see, create, change, and delete events on calendars you own, and to see your contacts. Birthdly only changes the birthday events it creates and never changes your contacts.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text19: Done. Your birthdays appear in your primary Google calendar within moments.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text20: Birthdly reads your contacts only to bring their birthdays into Birthdly and never changes them. In Google Calendar it changes only the birthday events it created itself.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text21: What the birthday events look like
googleCalendarBirthdays.text22: Each birthday is a Google birthday event that repeats every year, so it shows up just like the birthdays of your contacts.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text23: Every event has a reminder at 9:00 the day before, which gives you time to call or buy a present.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text24: Events are private and do not mark you as busy, so they never block meetings.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text25: A birthday on February 29 appears on February 28 in other years.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text26: People whose birthday comes from your Google Contacts do not get a second event, because Google already shows their birthday. You still see them in Birthdly.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text27: Keeping Birthdly and Google Calendar in sync
googleCalendarBirthdays.text28: Once connected, you can keep working in Birthdly and let it update Google:
googleCalendarBirthdays.text29: When you add a birthday in Birthdly or change its name or date, its event in Google Calendar changes too.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text30: When you delete a birthday in Birthdly, its event disappears from Google Calendar.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text31: When you delete one of Birthdly's birthday events in Google Calendar, Birthdly deletes that birthday as well.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text32: Birthdly checks Google for changes when you open the calendar, at most once an hour. To check right away, press Sync now in Settings.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text33: Google does not allow other edits to birthday events, such as changing the date in Google Calendar. Make those changes in Birthdly instead.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text35: Open Settings and press Disconnect on the Google Calendar card. Birthdly removes the birthday events it added to Google Calendar, and your birthdays stay in Birthdly. You can connect again at any time.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text37: Do I need a Birthdly account?
googleCalendarBirthdays.text38: You can add birthdays without an account. To sync with Google Calendar, sign in with Google, because the sync runs for your account on every device.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text39: Which calendar do the birthdays go to?
googleCalendarBirthdays.text40: Your primary Google calendar, the one named after your Google account.
googleCalendarBirthdays.text41: Will I see duplicates of my contacts' birthdays?
googleCalendarBirthdays.text42: Not when the name and birthday match. If a person has the same name and birthday in Birthdly and in Google Contacts, Birthdly links them instead of adding the person twice, and it does not create a second event. If the names differ, for example "Mom" in Birthdly and her full name in Google Contacts, you will see both. In that case, delete the one you added by hand in Birthdly.

intro.after: is a birthday calendar made for this job. You keep all birthdays in one list, with the relationship and notes such as gift ideas, and Birthdly adds them to Google Calendar as real birthday events.

birthdayReminders.title: How to get birthday reminders
birthdayReminders.description: Get a reminder on the day or the day before every birthday with Birthdly notifications and Google Calendar reminders.
birthdayReminders.text01: Most forgotten birthdays are not forgotten at all: you simply did not think of the date in time. A reminder the day before solves that, and it works best when it arrives on the device you already use. This guide shows how to get birthday reminders with Birthdly: as notifications from Birthdly itself, through Google Calendar, or both.
birthdayReminders.text02: What makes a good birthday reminder
birthdayReminders.text03: It comes early enough. The day before leaves time to send a card, order a gift, or plan a call.
birthdayReminders.text04: It comes where you look. A notification on your phone or computer works better than an app you have to open.
birthdayReminders.text05: It repeats every year on its own. You set up a birthday once and never touch it again.
birthdayReminders.text06: It is easy to keep complete. Reminders only help for the people you actually added.
birthdayReminders.text08: Birthdly keeps your list of birthdays and can remind you about them in two ways:
birthdayReminders.text09: Birthday notifications. Birthdly sends a browser notification with the birthdays of the day to every device where you turn them on. You choose whether it comes on the day, the day before, or both, and at what time. The notification arrives even when Birthdly is closed.
birthdayReminders.text10: Google Calendar. Birthdly adds each birthday to your Google Calendar as a birthday event with a reminder at 9:00 the day before. Google Calendar then shows that reminder wherever you are signed in to Google.
birthdayReminders.text11: Both need you to sign in with Google. You can use either one, or both at the same time.
birthdayReminders.text13: Sign in with Google using the account button in the top right corner.
birthdayReminders.text14: Turn on notifications. Open Settings, find Birthday notifications, and press Turn on for this device. When your browser asks, allow notifications.
birthdayReminders.text15: Choose when. Pick on the day, the day before, or both, and the time. These settings apply to all your devices. The time is in the time zone of the device where you last turned notifications on or changed these settings, shown under the controls.
birthdayReminders.text16: Notifications are turned on for each device separately, so repeat steps 2 and 3 on your phone and your computer. They cover every birthday in your account, including the ones imported from Google Contacts. Birthdays on the same day come together in one notification.
birthdayReminders.text17: On iPhone and iPad, notifications need iOS or iPadOS 16.4 or later. Add Birthdly to your Home Screen first: open it in Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. Open Birthdly from the Home Screen icon and turn on notifications there.
birthdayReminders.text18: If you blocked notifications for Birthdly earlier, the button does not appear. Allow them in your browser's site settings for Birthdly, then reload the page.
birthdayReminders.text20: Add birthdays and sign in with Google, as described above.
birthdayReminders.text21: Connect Google Calendar. Open Settings and press Connect Google Calendar. Birthdly creates a birthday event with a reminder for every birthday in your list, except the birthdays that come from your Google Contacts.
birthdayReminders.text22: Allow notifications for Google Calendar. On your phone, make sure notifications are turned on for the Google Calendar app. On a computer, allow notifications for Google Calendar in your browser.
birthdayReminders.text24: A reminder covers the next day or two. For a longer look ahead, use Birthdly itself:
birthdayReminders.text25: The Upcoming panel next to the calendar shows the next birthdays with labels such as "Tomorrow" or "in 5 days", and how old each person turns.
birthdayReminders.text26: The year view shows all birthdays of the year at once, which helps when you plan presents or trips.
birthdayReminders.text27: The People page lists everyone in one table that you can sort and search.
birthdayReminders.text28: Use the notes of a birthday for gift ideas. When the reminder arrives, open the person in Birthdly and the ideas are right there.
birthdayReminders.text30: Birthday notifications from Birthdly include the birthdays imported from your Google Contacts, like any other birthday in your account.
birthdayReminders.text31: Google Calendar already shows the birthdays saved in your Google Contacts, so Birthdly does not add a second event for them, and you do not get two reminders from Google Calendar. Its reminders for these birthdays follow its default notification settings for all-day events, so check those settings if you want a reminder for them too.
birthdayReminders.text32: Tips for never missing a birthday
birthdayReminders.text33: Add birthdays as soon as you hear them, even without the year. You can fill in the year later.
birthdayReminders.text34: Save the relationship, such as family, friends, or colleagues, so you can see at a glance who is who.
birthdayReminders.text35: Once a month, open the year view and check that nobody important is missing.
birthdayReminders.text37: Can Birthdly send me email reminders?
birthdayReminders.text38: Not at the moment. Birthdly sends browser notifications, and Google Calendar can remind you after you connect it.
birthdayReminders.text40: Birthday notifications arrive at the time you choose in Settings, 9:00 unless you change it, on the day, the day before, or both. Google Calendar reminders for birthdays you add in Birthdly arrive at 9:00 the day before, in the time zone of your Google Calendar. For birthdays from your Google Contacts, Google Calendar follows its own notification settings.
birthdayReminders.text41: Do I get reminders without connecting Google Calendar?
birthdayReminders.text42: Yes. Turn on birthday notifications in Settings. They do not depend on Google Calendar.
birthdayReminders.text43: Do notifications work when Birthdly is closed?
birthdayReminders.text44: Yes. You do not need to keep Birthdly open. On a computer, the browser itself needs to be running. If it is not, the notification arrives when you open the browser later that day.
birthdayReminders.text45: Will I get the same birthday twice?
birthdayReminders.text46: With On the day and the day before, the default, you hear about each birthday twice: the day before and on the day. Pick one of them in Settings if you want one notification. If you also connected Google Calendar, its reminder comes on top; turn off the reminder in Google Calendar, or turn off notifications for a device in Settings, if that is too much.

importFromGoogleContacts.title: How to import birthdays from Google Contacts
importFromGoogleContacts.description: Bring the birthdays saved in your Google Contacts into Birthdly, avoid duplicates, and keep them up to date without changing your contacts.
importFromGoogleContacts.text01: If you use Android or Gmail, many birthdays are probably already saved in your Google Contacts. Instead of typing them again, you can bring them into Birthdly in one step and keep them up to date automatically. This guide explains how the import works and what happens to your contacts.
importFromGoogleContacts.text03: You need a Google account with contacts that have a birthday saved.
importFromGoogleContacts.text04: Only contacts saved in your Google Contacts are imported. People you only emailed, which Google lists under "Other contacts", are not included.
importFromGoogleContacts.text05: A contact needs a name and at least the day and month of the birthday. The year is optional.
importFromGoogleContacts.text07: Open Settings and find the Google Calendar card.
importFromGoogleContacts.text08: Press Connect Google Calendar. Google shows two permissions: to see, create, change, and delete events on calendars you own, and to see your contacts. Birthdly only changes the birthday events it creates and never changes your contacts. Allow both.
importFromGoogleContacts.text09: Birthdly starts the first sync right away. After a short while, the birthdays of your contacts appear in the calendar and on the People page.
importFromGoogleContacts.text10: The import comes with the Google Calendar connection, so the same step also adds your Birthdly birthdays to Google Calendar with a reminder the day before.
importFromGoogleContacts.text12: Nothing. Birthdly only reads your contacts and never changes, adds, or deletes them. It reads the name and birthday of each contact and ignores everything else, such as phone numbers and email addresses.
importFromGoogleContacts.text14: If you added someone in Birthdly before importing, Birthdly tries to match them with your contacts. A person is matched when the name and the day and month of the birthday are the same and the birth years do not conflict; a missing year always matches, and letter case and extra spaces do not matter. A matched person stays one entry in Birthdly and keeps the relationship and notes you saved.
importFromGoogleContacts.text15: If the names differ, for example "Mom" in Birthdly and her full name in Google Contacts, Birthdly cannot tell they are the same person and you see two entries. Delete the one you added by hand in Birthdly.
importFromGoogleContacts.text16: Keeping imported birthdays up to date
importFromGoogleContacts.text17: Birthdly checks your contacts again when you open the calendar, at most once an hour, and when you press Sync now in Settings.
importFromGoogleContacts.text18: New contacts with a birthday are added to Birthdly.
importFromGoogleContacts.text19: A birthday or name changed in Google Contacts is updated in Birthdly, unless you edited that person in Birthdly more recently. Your latest edit wins.
importFromGoogleContacts.text20: A contact without a birth year never erases a year you already saved in Birthdly.
importFromGoogleContacts.text21: A birthday removed from a contact stays in Birthdly. From then on, Birthdly adds it to Google Calendar as its own birthday event.
importFromGoogleContacts.text23: While a contact still has a birthday in Google Contacts, deleting it in Birthdly does not last: the next sync imports it again. To remove such a birthday for good, first remove the birthday from the contact in Google Contacts, then delete it in Birthdly.
importFromGoogleContacts.text26: Can I import birthdays without connecting Google Calendar?
importFromGoogleContacts.text27: No. The import is part of the Google Calendar connection.
importFromGoogleContacts.text28: What happens to imported birthdays if I disconnect?
importFromGoogleContacts.text29: They stay in Birthdly. Disconnecting only removes the events Birthdly added to Google Calendar and stops the sync.
importFromGoogleContacts.text30: Can I add notes to imported birthdays?
importFromGoogleContacts.text31: Yes. Imported birthdays work like any other: you can set the relationship and add notes, such as gift ideas.
